en: Neither father, nor mother, nor kinsman, nor giver, nor son, nor daughter, nor servant, nor husband, nor wife, nor learning, nor livelihood—You alone are my refuge; You alone are my refuge; You alone are Bhavānī. ||1||

In the shoreless ocean of existence, I have fallen—fearful of great suffering, excessively greedy, alluring, and heedless—eternally bound by the snares of wretched saṃsāra; O Bhavānī, you alone are my refuge, you alone are my refuge, you alone are my refuge. 2.
I do not know charity nor the yoga of meditation; I do not know tantra nor hymns and mantras;
I do not know worship nor the yoga of ritual placement (nyāsa). You alone are my refuge, you alone are my refuge—O Bhavānī! ||3||
I do not know merit, nor do I know sacred fords; I never know liberation or dissolution.
I do not know devotion, nor even religious vows, O Mother; You are my refuge, You are my refuge, You alone are Bhavānī.
I am one of evil deeds, of evil associations, of evil intellect, of evil service, and devoid of noble conduct;
I am addicted to wicked behavior, possessed of false views, and bound by a web of evil speech. O Bhavānī, you alone are my refuge, you alone are my refuge, you alone are my sole resort. (5)
I never know the Lord of Creatures, the Lord of Ramā, the Great Lord, the Lord of Gods, the Lord of Day, or the Lord of Night;
nor do I know anything else. O Bhavānī, you alone are my refuge, you alone are my goal, you are the one who is ever my shelter. 6.

In dispute, in despair, in negligence, in exile, in water, in fire, on a mountain, in the midst of enemies, in the forest, or in need of refuge—always protect me; you are my resort, you are my resort; O Bhavānī, you alone are my sole refuge.
I am without a protector, poor, afflicted by old age and disease, utterly exhausted and wretched, with a face perpetually dull;
I have entered into calamity and am forever lost—You alone are my refuge, You alone are my refuge; be my sole resort. (8)
Thus ends the Bhavāny-aṣṭaka composed by the illustrious Śaṅkarācārya.
